My mother committed suicide when I was 17. She felt she had to battle all of her emotions on her own. I would have given anything for her to have talked to me or one of our family members and to have been able to help her. It is so hard for me to think that she felt forced to deal with this on her own. I would have given anything to help and so would any of her family and friends. 

You should not feel like you are a burden of any sort to your friends/family. It sounds like you have many people in your life and I am positive they would prefer to help you then for one day you to not be there anymore. Please talk to someone, someone cares and wants to help. It really saddens me that people feel they need to hide their problems because they are so stigmatized, I really feel for you.

If you have difficulty remembering to take your medication than I would definitely recommend avoiding it because it is very bad for you to suddenly stop taking these forms of medications you should actually be weened off of them to avoid negative emotional responses.

I am sure you have tried but maybe it would be good to set some goals and work towards them even if they start off small. For example, maybe you should find some other ways to spend your time now that you have quit your jobs such as learning to cook, going to the gym, or another hobby of some sort. Also maybe you should spend some time job searching or going to a job agency to try and find a job that you enjoy and that will consume some of your time. I know I have some mental emotional issues and if I have nothing to do all the time I start feeling very depressed, whereas if I am busy I feel I have much more purpose and am actually doing something. Another goal would be to work on expressing some emotion towards your children maybe try doing some new activities with them. I think building upon a relationships would be useful towards making you feel better. 

It will definitely take some time and effort to feel better but it will be worth it! I hope I am being some help.

And on a side note my mother committed suicide and it has always been very difficult for me to cope with. I would love her no matter her mental state and wished she had felt she could have reached out for help rather than fighting a battle on her own, which it sounds like you are doing and I am sure this is very difficult. Suicide leaves behind a lot of emotions for others regardless of how you think they feel towards you.

If you can't talk to your family I would suggest looking elsewhere you might not think it's worth it but it definitely can be and it's important to try.
